clue.text: Chap has to admit Damon's hellish good looking

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the chap's word takes the jumble inside it

parts.note: a chap is a he, a male person

indicators.note: something hellish is a wreck, so the name's letters come out in disorder

parts.note: the name with its possessive S, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A fan swoons that actor Matt Damon is devilishly attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in Damon's is not decoration: its S is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome describes a person with an attractive appearance, the same idea as good-looking.

clue.text: American lawyer volunteers information

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney, a US prosecutor
the TA, or Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A US attorney steps forward to offer facts to the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volunteers' reads as a verb but is a noun: the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time volunteer soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures collected for reference, a plain synonym for information.

clue.text: Steal back to the German frontier

indicators.note: going back means the word for steal is written from its end to its start

parts.note: to rob is to steal
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A thief sneaks back across to the German frontier with the loot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steal back' reads as recovering stolen goods, but 'back' only turns the theft word round.
explanation.definitionFit: A border is the boundary line between two countries, which is what a frontier is.

clue.text: Junk emails ultimately intend to deceive

indicators.note: junk is scrap to be broken up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the following word, keeping only its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of intend

explanation.surface: Spam messages are designed to trick the people who receive them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junk emails' looks like the everyday name for spam, but 'Junk' is a command to scramble the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislead someone is to give them a false impression, which is to deceive them.

clue.text: Storage here for prize committee

parts.note: a cup is a trophy, a prize
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: A cabinet is set aside to hold the trophy committee's papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storage here' means a place where things are stored, pointing at a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupboard is an enclosed cabinet with shelves where household items are kept.

clue.text: Prince has not taken up dance

parts.note: Charles was long the Prince of Wales

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means the word is lifted to read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The prince has refused to take up dancing lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: CHARLES plus NOT reversed (TON) gives CHARLESTON.
explanation.definitionFit: The Charleston is a lively 1920s dance named after the city in South Carolina.

clue.text: Struggle with husband being taken into service

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for with

indicators.note: something taken into another thing ends up inside it

parts.note: a rite is a religious service or ceremony
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A bride struggles as her husband is brought into the wedding service.
explanation.walkthrough: W comes first, then H sits inside RITE between T and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist and squirm, as when struggling against restraint or pain.

clue.text: I am about to eat a corn-ground pasta

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the words are read backwards
eating something takes it inside, so the reversed letters swallow the jumble

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: corn that is ground is milled to pieces, so these letters are broken and reformed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is about to tuck into pasta made from ground corn.
explanation.walkthrough: I AM reversed is MAI, and a rearrangement of A CORN goes between its A and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni is a kind of pasta shaped into short tubes.

clue.text: Guide woman into old city

indicators.note: one thing put into another sits inside it

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia, a crossword favourite
she refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A tour guide leads a woman into the ruins of an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur, the biblical city of Abraham, turns up constantly in crosswords as the 'old city'.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher guides people to their seats, so as a verb to usher is to guide.

clue.text: Advisor's first to get behind concept

indicators.note: the opening letter is told to move to the rear, so the word's front letter goes to its end

parts.note: an aide is an assistant or adviser

explanation.surface: A consultant's top priority is to support a new concept.
explanation.walkthrough: AIDE with its first letter A moved to the end becomes IDEA; 'to get behind' looks like 'to support'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought or notion formed in the mind, a direct synonym of concept.

clue.text: Meant to think over

definitions.meaning: first meaning: intentional, done on purpose
second meaning: to consider carefully before deciding

explanation.walkthrough: The word changes pronunciation between its two senses: an adjective ending '-it' and a verb ending '-ate'.
explanation.definitionFit: A deliberate act is intended, and to deliberate is to weigh a matter carefully before deciding.

clue.text: Baking apple has core replaced with fine filling

indicators.note: a filling goes inside, as in a pie or sandwich
letters replaced are put back in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
OK means fine, all right

explanation.surface: A baked apple has its core cut out and replaced with a tasty stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of CORE are rearranged as COER, and OK fills the middle. In Britain a cooker is also an apple grown for cooking rather than eating raw.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooker is the British name for a cooking apple, a sour variety such as a Bramley used in pies.

clue.text: Man covering for head gets honour from the Queen

parts.note: a knight is a chessman, one of the pieces
a hood covers the head

explanation.surface: A bareheaded man is awarded a royal honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a chess piece here; KNIGHT plus HOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A knighthood is the title of Sir conferred by the monarch as a royal award.

clue.text: Came to a funeral feast and downed half

parts.note: taken as written
a wake is a gathering, often with food and drink, held after a death

indicators.note: keeping only half means the other half of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mourner went to the funeral gathering and drank too much.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the second half of DOWNED, NED, is kept. 'Came to' means regained consciousness, not arrived at.
explanation.definitionFit: To be awakened is to have regained consciousness, which is what coming to means after a faint.

clue.text: Sets about grabbing kiss that is most arousing!

indicators.note: grabbing something holds it inside a grip
moved about means shifted around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
X is the conventional symbol for a kiss
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A seductive embrace with a snatched kiss is the most thrilling moment.
explanation.walkthrough: SETS rearranged to SEST holds X and IE in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexiest is the superlative of sexy, meaning causing the greatest sexual excitement.

clue.text: Pay out endlessly to acquire rodents raised as sample

indicators.note: acquiring something takes it in, so one part holds the other
without an end, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to spend is to pay out money

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means lifted to read from bottom to top

parts.note: mice are small rodents

explanation.surface: A lab pays out to buy rodents bred for testing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' suggests rodents bred in a lab, but in a down clue it turns the word upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is an individual example taken for study, which is a sample.

clue.text: Indie to run with copy

indicators.note: letters that run like dye bleed out of place, ending in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An independent publisher is about to print a run of copies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks like a print run, but it tells you to rearrange the letters of INDIE TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A copy of a book or newspaper is one edition, a single issue of a printing.

clue.text: Contestant not losing heart after abysmal pop single

indicators.note: after places one part following the other in the answer
something abysmal is a mess, so the letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
single means one

indicators.note: a word that loses its heart keeps only its outside letters

parts.note: the outer letters of not

explanation.surface: A talent show contestant stays upbeat despite releasing a terrible pop single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' is not a record here but the number one, joined to pop before the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent is someone you compete against, and a contestant is one who competes.

clue.text: Sh! Live Question Time broadcast has minute to go

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, like seed thrown across a field
something that has to go is removed, here the letter for a minute

parts.note: to be is to live, to exist
QU is the abbreviation for question
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: A shushing call goes out as a live political panel show goes on air.
explanation.walkthrough: Question Time is a BBC political debate programme; TIME without M is TIE, rearranged as IET.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Sh!' is the sound you make to tell someone to stop talking, the same command as be quiet.

clue.text: Pool money before getting expensive wool

indicators.note: before puts the money word ahead of the pool word

parts.note: cash is money
a mere is a small lake or pond

explanation.surface: Friends club together for a pricey woollen garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pool money' reads as clubbing together, but Pool is a pond word that comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is fine, costly wool from the undercoat of Kashmir goats.

clue.text: Prayer's no good — energy's required to get even

parts.note: an Ave Maria is a Catholic prayer
NG abbreviates no good
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Prayer is useless; it takes energy to settle the score.
explanation.definitionFit: To avenge a wrong is to take revenge for it, which is getting even.

clue.text: Cover for work in prison yard

indicators.note: in means placed inside the following words

parts.note: the can is slang for prison
op is short for opus, a work
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: Shelter is put up for inmates working in the exercise yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In prison yard' reads as a location, but 'in' places the work between prison and yard; the can is US slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy is an overhead covering, such as a cloth roof over a bed or stall.

clue.text: Give role to the French man

parts.note: to cast an actor is to give them a role
le is a French word for the

explanation.surface: A director gives a part to the Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French man' looks like one person, but 'man' alone is the definition: a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle, or rook, is one of the pieces, called men, in chess.

clue.text: Applied skills to bake ten quiches

indicators.note: baking transforms ingredients into something new, so the letters are recombined

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cookery student puts practical skills to use baking ten quiches.
explanation.definitionFit: Techniques are practical methods of doing a task, the skills a craftsperson puts to use.

clue.text: Path is part of guerrilla network

indicators.note: being part of means the letters are found within the run of words

parts.note: letters inside the phrase across its word gap

explanation.surface: A trail belongs to a secret supply route used by rebel fighters.
explanation.definitionFit: A lane is a narrow road or track, a kind of path.

clue.text: Tax Mississippi bank, say

indicators.note: say asks us to hear the word spoken rather than read it

parts.note: a levee is an embankment built along the Mississippi river

explanation.surface: A duty is charged on goods landed at a riverbank in Mississippi.
explanation.walkthrough: Levee and levy are pronounced the same in standard British English.
explanation.definitionFit: A levy is a charge imposed by authority, which is a tax.

clue.text: Turn round and almost see bird

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word stops short of its last letter

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game
O is round in shape
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone turns around and nearly spots a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn round' looks like one phrase, but splits into a go and the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A goose is a large waterbird related to ducks and swans.

clue.text: Cheers seven-nil slaughter!

indicators.note: a slaughter leaves things torn apart, so the letters are scattered and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: Fans celebrate a seven-nil thrashing of their rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' looks like a noun for applause, but it is a verb meaning brightens up.
explanation.definitionFit: To enliven someone is to cheer them up, making them livelier and happier.
